slides.1.title: Three routes to Greek sweetness
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Sun-drying
slides.1.highlights.0.content: e.g. Santorini Vinsanto, Lemnos sweet reds from sun-dried grapes, Samos Nectar
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Fortification
slides.1.highlights.1.content: e.g. Mavrodaphne of Patras (sweet fortified red) and Samos Vin Doux Naturel
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Aromatic varieties
slides.1.content: In Diploma comparisons, first ask how the sweetness arose: drying, fortification, or both.
slides.2.title: Mavrodaphne of Patras
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Grapes
slides.2.highlights.0.content: At least 51% Mavrodaphne, the rest Black Corinthian
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Ageing
slides.2.highlights.1.content: At least one year in oak of no more than 1,000 litres; Reserve is two years in oak plus one in bottle; Grand Reserve seven years in total (at least three in barrel)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: A 1971 appellation
slides.2.highlights.2.content: In north-central Achaia, with sub-zones including Rio
slides.2.content: The representative sweet fortified red, often compared stylistically with Port and Banyuls.
slides.3.title: The Muscat and Malvasia families
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Muscat
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Samos, Patras, Rio Patras, Rhodes, Lemnos and Cephalonia all have Muscat PDOs; Lemnos and Samos use different Muscats (Alexandria vs Blanc à Petits Grains)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Malvasia
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Monemvasia-Malvasia, Malvasia Candia, Malvasia Sitia and Malvasia Paros
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Memory aid
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Muscat = aromatic sweet wines of the islands and Patras; Malvasia = historic name, Crete, Paros, Monemvasia
slides.3.content: Memorise place-to-sweet-wine pairs first; details follow in Level 3 comparison questions.

slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
What type of wine is Mavrodaphne of Patras?
A sweet fortified red led by Mavrodaphne.
How are Santorini Vinsanto grapes handled?
Dried, then aged oxidatively in oak.
A. Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
Lemnos uses Muscat of Alexandria; Samos uses Blanc à Petits Grains.
